display_name: Staples Hyken Ergonomic Mesh Swivel Task Chair, Black (ST63137)
claim_policy_note: Not a regulated product, so the claim lint logs rather than blocks. Every string in this config nonetheless traces to the brief's Front-of-Pack copy, its Product Attributes field, the spec sheet's measured dimensions, or the Asset Tracker's live listing copy. Nothing is invented. `text_provenance` is recorded per shot.

ORIGINATION_NOTE.what_was_originated: The SHOT STRUCTURE only - which six shots, which stack template each uses, and which approved string goes on which shot.
ORIGINATION_NOTE.what_was_NOT_originated: Not one word of copy. Every rendered string is verbatim from the brief, the spec sheet or the live listing. The chair is the one SKU where the client supplied plenty of approved language but no shot list, so structure was the only gap.
ORIGINATION_NOTE.template_selection_basis: Section 8 of the Staples Digital Content Style Guide, restricted to the templates whose 'When to use' text applies to furniture. The guide names furniture explicitly for Dimensions and for Comparison vs self, and names a room scene as the case where scale matters - so those drove the plan.
ORIGINATION_NOTE.flag_for_client: Every shot below carries `originated: true`. Surface that in the UI or the package README so Sandeep can see which shots were our editorial call rather than his brief's.

dimensions_source_of_truth._note: DECIDED 2026-09-15 by Pratyoosh: use the FLOOR-REFERENCED figures, matching Staples' own dimensions infographic. Do not mix these with the spec sheet's panel-height figure.
dimensions_source_of_truth.source: Asset Tracker row 4 spec attributes, cross-checked against the spec sheet's 'Chair Dimension' sheet row 15 ('Claimed (in)', averaged across 10 factory test samples) and against Staples' own finished 'Bynder default-990119_Dims.png'. All three agree to the tenth of an inch on every figure except back height - see below.

do_NOT_use.why: The spec sheet's 'Back Height' measures the backrest PANEL itself. The Asset Tracker's 28.3-29.1 in measures the backrest top FROM THE FLOOR. Both are correct; they measure different things. Staples' published infographic uses the floor-referenced figure, and mixing the two in one graphic would produce a chart that contradicts itself.

scene_prompt.template: A clean product photograph on a pure white seamless background showing a black mesh-back ergonomic office task chair with an attached headrest, adjustable armrests and a polished five-star base with casters, seen straight on from the front, centered and occupying the middle half of the frame's width. The chair must match the reference image exactly in color, material, proportion and geometry - black mesh back and seat, black plastic armrests with silver accents, polished aluminium base. Even, soft, shadowless studio lighting with a faint contact shadow. No text, no labels, no props, no people, no background elements. IMPORTANT: keep a generous margin of clean, empty, pure white space down the full left edge and the full right edge of the frame - roughly the outer quarter on each side must be completely empty. These margins are reserved for callout graphics that will be added afterwards, so no part of the chair may extend into them.

Mesh weave is a material detail, and 'Breathable Mesh' is the brief's own Anchor Bar Differentiator for this SKU - the single thing Staples chose to lead on.

scene_prompt.template: A photorealistic interior scene: a black mesh-back ergonomic office task chair with an attached headrest and a polished five-star base, positioned at a three-quarter angle beside a light oak desk in a bright modern home office. A window with sheer curtains sits on the right letting in soft warm daylight; the wall is white, the floor is pale wide-plank wood with a neutral woven rug under the desk. A closed laptop and a small potted plant sit on the desk. The chair must match the reference image exactly in color, material, proportion and geometry - black mesh back and seat, black armrests with silver accents, polished aluminium base with casters. Warm, inviting color grading. Walls white or light gray, furniture in light woods. No people. No visible brand logos anywhere in the scene. No competitor branding, no signage, no readable text of any kind. IMPORTANT: leave the entire upper-left third of the frame as clean, uncluttered, evenly-lit plain white wall with no objects, no shelving, no artwork, no strong texture and no busy detail - this area is reserved for a text headline that will be added afterwards.

shots.purpose: Human context and in use. A person seated and working, conveying fit, posture and lumbar support.
shots.template_justification: Style guide, section 8.2: 'Placing a person in the frame to communicate size and real-world relevance.' For a chair the person is not optional decoration - it is the only way to show fit and posture, which is what the lumbar and ergonomic claims are about.

pipeline_mix.note: v1.2 demo mix: hero + dimensions graphic (furniture needs exact specs) + four photo_overlay education/lifestyle frames + one photo_only commercial work-life scene. No trust/certifications graphic card.

candidate_shots_considered_and_rejected.why_rejected: The guide's own example is 'different models of office chairs', and Staples has a finished 'HYKEN FAMILY' image comparing Hyken / Hyken Pro / Hyken XL. Strong fit - but it requires accurate hero imagery for the Pro and XL models, which are different SKUs not in this folder. Generating a plausible-looking Pro or XL would be inventing a product. Enable only if Staples supplies those heroes.

The Asset Tracker says 'Assembly required' and 'Full Assembly Required', but the guide says to use this template only when 'the ease of assembly is part of the value proposition'. Nothing in the brief or the listing frames assembly as a benefit - it is disclosed, not sold. Using it would invert the client's own positioning.
The guide's case is a product that 'visibly changes a customer's environment'. A chair replacing a chair is not a visible environmental change in the way a desk organizer or a floor cleaner is.
Pack inclusion is '1 chair'. Nothing to enumerate.

Tempting, because the brief is a REBRAND/REPACK project and Bullet_Copy_1 is literally 'PACKAGING MAY VARY, SAME GREAT PRODUCT.' But the old packaging artwork is not in this folder, so an old-vs-new shot cannot be built truthfully. Worth raising with Sandeep - if he supplies the old artwork this becomes a genuinely good shot, and it addresses a real customer confusion.
